newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy meets Albanian rebels, deal reported.
newsitem.headline: Italy meets Albanian rebels, deal reported.

text.p: An Italian envoy met leaders of the uprising from the southern Albanian port of Vlore on Monday and Italian media said the rebel representatives had undertaken to encourage civilians to lay down their weapons.

An Italian Foreign Ministry statement said the talks were held in the Adriatic on the amphibious assault ship San Giorgio between Italy's ambassador to Albania, Paolo Foresti, and rebel representatives.

The news agency ANSA and RAI television, reporting from on board the vessel, said the eight representatives had signed a declaration with Foresti undertaking "to ensure public order and progessively restore normal administration" to the town.
ANSA said the declaration asked for Italian and international emergency aid and undertook "to favour the immediate handing back of weapons in the hands of the citizens of Vlore".

The rebel representatives had also sought "guarantees" that an agreement signed by Albanian President Sali Berisha and political parties in Tirana on Sunday to resolve the crisis peacefully would be applied correctly and rapidly.
The Foreign Ministry could not immediately confirm the media reports and further details were not available.
Vlore is at the epicentre of an armed insurrection in southern Albania, where anti-government rebels who have stormed state armouries are in control through most of the region.
Berisha, his ruling Democratic Party and nine opposition parties signed an agreement on Sunday aimed at securing a political solution to the conflict.

The accord provides for an all-party government and new elections by June under international supervision. It gives rebels a week to hand in their weapons and asks parliament to declare an amnesty for all those implicated in the revolt.
Rebels have insisted on the resignation of Berisha, whom they blamed for allowing pyramid investment schemes to flourish before collapsing with the savings of hundreds of thousands.

Monday's Italian statement said "the authorities in Tirana have asked the Italian government's cooperation in initiating a dialogue with representatives of the movements operating in Vlore and other towns in the south" of Albania.
The request had been made "in order to consolidate and hasten" implementation of the Tirana agreement, it said.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini visited Tirana on Sunday night shortly after the deal was signed. He said after meeting Berisha and the opposition that Italy had been asked to underwrite the accord and monitor its application.

Monday's statement said the rebel representatives, ferried to the San Giorgio by helicopter, had been told by Foresti that Italy was ready to supply humanitarian aid and, with the European Union, help to revive Albania's shattered economy.
Italy, which briefly occupied Albania under Fascism in World War Two, has strong cultural and commercial links with the Balkan state, Europe's poorest country.
It has been active in seeking a peaceful end to the unrest and has bolstered its military presence in the Adriatic out of fear that all-out war could trigger an exodus of refugees.

Italy has evacuated 78 foreigners from Vlore in the past week in three rescue missions using military helicopters. The latest airlift on Monday brought out six Italians, two Albanians, a German and an American, the foreign ministry said.
